note: Cross-cutting accommodations and delivery adjustments. These apply ON TOP OF any population profile; they are NOT populations and NEVER label a learner by a condition (SCHEMAS design law 6). Each modifier names what to DO, and maps to the existing learner-profile `supports` vocabulary (SCHEMAS section 5) and/or a delivery constraint. MP-11/MP-02/MP-04 read them from CONFIG.modifiers and apply them to rendering and delivery, not to shared `core` identity.

modifiers.name: Screen-reader friendly
modifiers.description: Rendered so a screen reader conveys everything a sighted reader gets.
rendering_rules: No symbol without its spoken form (write 'one quarter' or give the words beside the glyph).
No information carried by a table's visual layout alone; linearise it.
Every image needs a text alternative; never put meaning only in a figure.
modifiers.what_if_wrong: A bare symbol or a layout-only table is silently dropped by a screen reader, so the learner loses the point without knowing it. Pair every glyph with words and linearise tables.

modifiers.name: Dyslexia-friendly text
modifiers.description: Text shaped to reduce decoding load, without changing the content or singling anyone out.
rendering_rules: Short paragraphs, one idea each; generous spacing.
Plain words; define or avoid long low-frequency terms.
No large blocks of italics or all-caps; at most one emphasis per paragraph.
modifiers.what_if_wrong: Dense justified text with heavy emphasis raises decoding effort and the learner stops. Keep chunks short and emphasis sparse. Never record this as a diagnosis about the learner.

modifiers.name: Captions and transcripts
modifiers.description: Every audio or video segment carries synchronised captions and a full text transcript.
rendering_rules: Any audio/video delivery MUST ship a transcript the learner can read instead.
Captions carry speaker turns and meaningful non-speech sound.
The transcript is the source of truth when bandwidth drops the media.
modifiers.what_if_wrong: Uncaptioned media excludes anyone who cannot hear it or cannot play it; the lesson becomes undeliverable. Always provide the transcript as a text fallback.

modifiers.name: Low-vision friendly
modifiers.description: Presentation that stays usable at large text sizes and high contrast.
rendering_rules: No meaning carried by colour alone; pair colour with a label or shape.
Clear heading structure so a magnifier user keeps their place.
Reflowable text; never fix content to a width that breaks when enlarged.
modifiers.what_if_wrong: Colour-only cues and fixed-width layouts vanish or break under magnification. Label cues and keep text reflowable.

modifiers.name: Low-bandwidth delivery
modifiers.description: Content that loads and teaches with almost no network.
rendering_rules: Text-first; heavy media is optional and never required to meet an objective.
Every media element has a text equivalent that stands alone.
Keep each lesson small enough to fetch once on a weak connection.
modifiers.what_if_wrong: A lesson that needs a video to make sense is unreachable on a weak link. Make text carry the objective and treat media as a bonus.

modifiers.name: Offline and printable first
modifiers.description: Each lesson works with no connectivity and prints to paper without loss.
rendering_rules: No step depends on a live service, link or lookup.
A printable one-page form carries the whole objective.
Interactivity has a paper fallback (write the answer, a volunteer checks).
modifiers.what_if_wrong: A lesson that assumes connectivity or a screen cannot run in a crisis or under-resourced setting. Give every lesson a self-contained printable form.
